clue.text: Copper has to come down hard on unroadworthy vehicle?

parts.note: copper is a reddish-brown colour, like rust
to bucket down is to rain heavily

explanation.surface: A police officer has to crack down on a car unfit for the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a colour, RUST; to 'bucket' (down) is British for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an old, corroded car that is barely fit to be driven.

clue.text: Princes brought up to serve, in the beginning

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed or nearly so, i.e. ajar

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word serve is used

explanation.surface: Royal sons raised to be servants from an early age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is the adverb in 'push the door to', nearly shut, hence AJAR; 'brought up' turns it to RAJA, then S starts 'serve'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rajas are Indian princes or kings, the title used across the subcontinent.

clue.text: Delivered after expiry date?

parts.note: reads like goods arriving past their use-by date, but describes a baby born after it has already died

explanation.definitionFit: A baby delivered dead is born after its life has expired, so the clue is a sideways description.

clue.text: Corruptly harbour negligence? Not our place to expose material

indicators.note: corruptly means the letters of the following words are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word our is what must be left out, as 'Not our' signals

explanation.surface: An accusation that a port authority has been corruptly negligent, and the matter is none of our business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corruptly' rearranges HARBOUR NEGLIGENCE once OUR is removed ('Not our'); the remaining fourteen letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleaching green is a grassy patch where washed linen was spread out in the sun to whiten.

clue.text: Obscure? Call it up in computer

parts.note: to call out is to cry

indicators.note: the reversed word is set inside the computer abbreviation

parts.note: PC, personal computer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read upwards

explanation.surface: A puzzling message: is it obscure, so call it up on the computer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the pronoun backwards before 'in' places it inside the computer abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic and obscure are synonyms: both describe meaning that is hidden or hard to grasp.

clue.text: Film studios' lines for American actor

parts.note: an el is an American elevated railway line
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous actor-manager

explanation.surface: A film company's script lines are handed to an American star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' attaches to 'lines', not 'actor': ELS are US elevated railways. TREE is the Victorian actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree in Hertfordshire is home to well-known British film and television studios.

clue.text: Sort of bike seen in yard

definitions.meaning: a four-wheeled motorbike for rough ground
a quadrangle, the enclosed courtyard of a college

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are short forms: quad bike, and quadrangle for an enclosed court.

clue.text: Places seeing early growth brought in computerisation

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Offices where new technology took hold first when computers arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs are where a foetus grows in its earliest stage of life.

clue.text: Casual friendship brings marriage to daughter

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between two families

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a light friendship leading to a daughter's wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a light, uncommitted flirtation or affair, not a serious bond.

clue.text: Bulgarian ruler is reformed terrorist

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Balkan leader who has mended his ways was once a terrorist.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban guerrilla is a terrorist or insurgent fighting in cities rather than the countryside.

clue.text: Sluggish, wasting time aboard pleasure craft

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed on board, inside the other

parts.note: pleasure is joy

indicators.note: wasting means the time abbreviation is thrown away

parts.note: sluggish means inert

explanation.surface: A lazy passenger whiles away the hours on a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pleasure craft' looks like one unit but splits: 'craft' is the definition. 'wasting' drops the time letter from the sluggish word, and the remainder goes 'aboard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joinery is the woodworking craft of making doors, windows and fittings.

clue.text: A fifty for county tailender would be strange

indicators.note: for means one letter is replaced by the other pieces

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A tailend batsman scoring a half-century for his county would be a strange event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailender' names the Y at the end of SURREY, which A L replaces. In cricket a tailender is a weak batsman near the end of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something bizarre and dreamlike, so it means strange.

clue.text: Will composer ask for another to drop fortissimo?

parts.note: to solicit is to ask for something

indicators.note: to drop means that musical abbreviation is let fall from the word

parts.note: F (ff) marks fortissimo, very loud, in music

explanation.surface: Would a composer, will he ask someone else to drop the very loud passages?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will composer' is not a musician but someone who drafts wills; 'another' just adds that the request is made on another's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is a lawyer who among other things draws up people's wills.

clue.text: Excuse totally for cutting book in two

indicators.note: cutting trims the final letter off the word

parts.note: all means totally

indicators.note: the book letter goes inside the two

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone excuses a book being cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' shortens ALL to AL; B goes 'in' II for IBI.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: Oil sprinkled on second radish

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: sprinkled means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil drizzled on a second radish salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooli is a long white radish, also called daikon.

clue.text: With hard line leader changing turning out sloppily

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taking a hawkish line means being hard-line

explanation.surface: A hardliner's leader is replaced, and things turn out in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say what the new first letter is: 'leader changing' swaps H for a letter that only the definition settles, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy can mean gushing and sentimental, which is the sense of mawkish.

clue.text: Minister runs and exercises in spotless clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the word surrounds the others like a garment

parts.note: spotless means clean
R stands for runs in cricket
gym is exercises

explanation.surface: A government minister jogs and works out in immaculate kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a minister of religion, a priest or pastor.

clue.text: Fools terribly dim, I guess

indicators.note: terribly means the letters are badly mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are very stupid, they suppose.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to mislead them, as misguides does.

clue.text: What suitor hopes to do holding say, flute?

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a suitor hopes to win a lass
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An admirer hopes to win his girl while holding a champagne flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute is a tall, narrow glass for champagne or wine.

clue.text: He blames one for exploiting cricket club?

parts.note: a means one
a user is one who exploits

explanation.surface: A man is blamed for taking advantage of a cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is a person who charges or blames another.

clue.text: Greek island's sent round a lot of spicy food

indicators.note: sent round means the word surrounds the letter

parts.note: Samos is a Greek island; Samos's

explanation.surface: Someone from a Greek island posts round a lot of hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are spicy fried pastries, so a lot of them make a lot of spicy food.

clue.text: Unmarried blokes with girl to follow

indicators.note: unmarried means the married abbreviation is removed

parts.note: blokes are men
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Single men chase a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried' removes M, the abbreviation for married, from MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a result.

clue.text: Turkish port is just in sound

indicators.note: in sound signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: 'is mere' means is just

explanation.surface: A Turkish harbour lies right on a channel of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a sea channel by the port but signals that 'is mere' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a major port city on Turkey's Aegean coast.

clue.text: Pale and spotty, son needs to get out

indicators.note: the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: measles gives a spotty rash, so measly means spotty

explanation.surface: A pallid, spotty boy needs to go outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealy can describe a pale, floury complexion.

clue.text: Visit to be revived

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to pop in on someone and to wake after fainting.

clue.text: Whiskey in Kildare maybe that could blow your head!

indicators.note: the whiskey goes inside the doctor's title

parts.note: Dr Kildare was a fictional television doctor, an example of a DR
rye is a whiskey

explanation.surface: Irish whiskey from County Kildare packs a punch fit to blow your head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kildare' looks like the Irish county but is Dr Kildare, doctor hero of a 1960s TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdryer blows hot air over your head; the exclamation adds the joke.

clue.text: Goodness has never failed? That's not right

indicators.note: failed means the letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thank goodness, it has never gone wrong? That's not true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' is the anagram signal; 'That's not right' removes the right abbreviation from the pool first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'Goodness me!' or 'Good heavens!'

clue.text: Forged gold blocks agent spotted

indicators.note: blocks means one piece stops up the middle of the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape

explanation.surface: Fake gold stops a spy who has been seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' scrambles the metal, and 'blocks' puts it in the middle of the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Splodgy means marked with blotches, so spotted fits.

clue.text: Idle youth repeatedly abandoning books for toy

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is given twice
abandoning means the books letter is dropped

parts.note: a yob is a loutish youth
B is an abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A lazy boy keeps leaving his books for a plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: YOB, a British slang word for a lout, loses its B for YO, which is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spool toy that climbs and falls on a string.

clue.text: Intruder in boudoir finally put on Frenchwoman's very old hat

parts.note: tres is French for very
passe means out of date, old hat

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An intruder in a lady's bedroom tries on a French woman's dated hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' means R goes after: in a charade it is joined to the end. 'old hat' means out of fashion, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone who enters land or property without permission.
